title: Silas and the Vow
premise: Wendell Fairweather, a ghostwriter who buries his own voice in other people's stories, is hired to write the memoirs of celebrated novelist Silas Vane—unaware that Silas is the estranged brother of Marlowe, the woman Wendell once loved and lost. When Marlowe begs him to pose as her date at the Fairweather family reunion to deflect her mother's matchmaking, old wounds and new truths collide over a single long weekend. As Wendell's manuscript forces both siblings to confront the betrayal that split their family, he must choose between professional loyalty and the second chance he never believed he deserved. The story ends with Wendell publishing his first book under his own name and choosing Marlowe—not because timing improved, but because they finally forgave themselves enough to stop waiting for it.
about_author: Hazel Halloran is a former wedding planner from coastal Maine who traded seating charts for love stories after a decade of watching people say yes. She writes warm, wry romances about people who arrive late to their own lives.

chapters.title: The Ghost in the Manuscript
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. He accepts a lucrative, anonymous contract to ghostwrite a famous novelist's memoirs, hiding the client's name even from his agent. The emotional beat: quiet self-erasure—he's good at disappearing, and it's starting to cost him.

chapters.title: Terms and Conditions
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. At the first interview, he discovers his subject is Silas Vane—and that Silas's sister is Marlowe Fairweather, the woman who walked out of his life seven years ago. Beat: dread disguised as professionalism.

chapters.title: Seven Years of Bad Timing
chapters.summary: Marlowe's POV. She runs a struggling bookshop and has just learned her brother's memoir will expose the family's oldest wound. She needs armor for Sunday's reunion. Beat: panic sharpening into a reckless idea.

chapters.title: A Favor Between Strangers
chapters.summary: Marlowe's POV. She asks Wendell to be her fake date; he agrees before pride can object. Their negotiation crackles with unfinished history neither will name. Beat: reluctant hope.

chapters.title: The Reunion
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The Fairweather house brims with aunts, rivalries, and Marlowe's mother's merciless scrutiny. The fake couple performs flawlessly—too flawlessly. Beat: the past becoming dangerously comfortable.

chapters.title: Dessert
chapters.summary: Marlowe's POV. Over lemon cake, her mother toasts them as a couple, and neither corrects her. A stolen moment on the porch ends almost in a kiss. Beat: the lie turning sweet.

chapters.title: Chapter One of Somebody Else
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Back at Silas's estate, interviews reveal the brother-sister rupture: Silas's bestselling debut stole its central story from Marlowe's life without permission. Beat: Wendell realizes he's writing the weapon.

chapters.title: What Silas Wants
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Ill and running out of time, Silas insists the memoir include everything—the theft, the guilt, the apology he never delivered. He wants reconciliation more than reputation. Beat: a dying man's honesty.

chapters.title: Second Date, First Truth
chapters.summary: Marlowe's POV. To keep up appearances, she and Wendell have a 'real' date. Wine loosens the truth about why she left him: she was pregnant, grieving, and couldn't bear being seen. Beat: grief finally spoken aloud.

chapters.title: The Draft
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. His draft chapter on the stolen novel is devastatingly good—and Marlowe, editing her brother's publicity materials, reads it by accident. Beat: betrayal by proxy; she feels exposed twice.

chapters.title: Confrontation at the Bookshop
chapters.summary: Marlowe's POV. She accuses Wendell of selling her pain again, this time to the same man. He can't defend the contract without breaking confidentiality. Beat: love against duty, first collision.

chapters.title: Silas Intervenes
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Learning of the fallout, Silas summons both of them and confesses the theft directly, asking Marlowe to read the final chapter before judging it. Beat: humility from an unlikely source.

chapters.title: The Unread Chapter
chapters.summary: Marlowe's POV. She refuses to read it. Wendell, caught between them, offers to walk away from the biggest contract of his career. Beat: the cost of loyalty made concrete.

chapters.title: Mother Knows
chapters.summary: Marlowe's POV. Her mother reveals she knew the romance was staged from the start—and that she remembers young Wendell, and what Marlowe gave up. Beat: maternal truth-telling that cuts and heals at once.

chapters.title: Deadline
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Silas is hospitalized; the publisher moves the memoir's release up, threatening to run the raw draft—including the chapter Marlowe forbade. Beat: ticking clock engaged.

chapters.title: Breaking Confidentiality
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Wendell makes his choice: he gives Marlowe the manuscript, breaching his contract, and tells Silas why. Beat: duty inverted—loyalty to people over paper.

chapters.title: The Apology
chapters.summary: Marlowe's POV. In a hospital room, Marlowe finally reads the last chapter: not an exploitation but an elegy, ending with Silas asking forgiveness and giving her back her story. Beat: catharsis.

chapters.title: The Person in the Mirror
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Silas dies peacefully days later. Wendell, hollowed out, confronts his own habit of hiding—every book unsigned, every feeling deferred. Beat: the real antagonist revealed as himself.

chapters.title: What the Will Left Behind
chapters.summary: Marlowe's POV. Silas's will names Marlowe co-trustee of his literary legacy and asks Wendell—by name—to finish the memoir under his own byline. Beat: posthumous blessing; found family formalized.

chapters.title: Bylines
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. At the memorial reading, Wendell publicly claims the memoir and, for the first time, his own name. Marlowe watches from the front row. Beat: identity reclaimed.

chapters.title: No More Fake Dates
chapters.summary: Marlowe's POV. Weeks later, Marlowe asks Wendell on a date—no pretense, no family audience, just two people trying again. He says yes before she finishes the sentence. Beat: joy without armor.

chapters.title: Silas and the Vow
chapters.summary: Alternating POV epilogue. The memoir publishes to acclaim; Marlowe's shop hosts the launch, her mother in attendance, Silas's letter read aloud. On the porch where they almost kissed, Wendell proposes—not with perfect timing, but with perfect willingness. Beat: second chances kept, not waited for.
